newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm as direction sought.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm as direction sought.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Friday were steady to firmer amid trader caution over market direction, traders said on Friday.
Singapore swaps provided little direction with September talked marginally firmer with bids at $110.50, from Thursday's $109/$109.75.
"It is relatively firm ... stocks are still low and there are not a lot of AG cargoes," a trader said.
But traders said there would be more Gulf supplies in the second half of September.
"If prices here remain so strong, we can expect a lot more cargoes," said a Singapore trader.
South Korean cargoes were also being offered into Singapore as Chinese enquiries have been vague, traders said.
Some traders said Singapore 180-cst prices should find support at above $110 following a rally up to $116 earlier this week on U.S./Iraq tensions.
On Thursday 180-cst fuel oil was assessed at $111/$113 per tonne and 380-cst was assessed at $107/$109.
More fuel oil was also expected to be moved through increased bunker sales as shipowners on Friday were cornered to buying prior to the weekend after having been quiet the whole week, traders said.
